PLAY TIME
45–60 seconds

GOAL
Track patterns using single-vote observables.

ONE RULE
READ INPUT — Read input with onevote-boxhold: what happened first. · onevote-boxhold

PLAY
READ OUTPUT — Read output through onevote-boxhold: leave motives blank. · onevote-boxhold

TWIST
ONE VOTE — In onevote-boxhold, count each clue once. · onevote-boxhold
SUSPEND — In onevote-boxhold, hold output without obedience. · onevote-boxhold
CHOOSE — From onevote-boxhold, take one chosen move. · onevote-boxhold

WIN
Control paused through repeat-neutral holding.

MIND BEND
Single-vote patterns survive wrong stories.

SAFETY
SAFETY CHECK · LOW-INTENSITY SAFETY
USE ONLY IF — You are working with automatic-pattern blindness, can stay oriented to the present, can think clearly enough to choose, and can stop at any time.
STOP NOW IF — Keep moral language where clear ethical wrongdoing must be named.
DO INSTEAD — End the round, orient to the room, slow the pace, and choose one simple grounding or practical action. If distress keeps rising, involve a trusted person or qualified professional.

Australia: call 000. For 24/7 crisis support in Australia, call Lifeline 13 11 14 or text 0477 13 11 14. Outside Australia, use your local emergency or crisis service.
This is self-help guidance, not diagnosis, treatment, or emergency care.

rituals.primary_trigger: Your thoughts or perceptions feel frightening or hard to verify in the moment
rituals.recognition_cue: Your thoughts or perceptions feel frightening or hard to verify in the moment
rituals.immediate_need: Stop analysing the frightening experience and say the sentence that gets live help involved.
rituals.safety:
SAFETY CHECK · SUPPORT-FIRST SAFETY
USE ONLY IF — This is not ordinary self-help. Use it only as a bridge to safe human or urgent support.
STOP NOW IF — There is immediate danger, self-harm or violence risk, a possible medical emergency, frightening loss of shared reality, or you cannot stay safe.
DO INSTEAD — Stop self-help and involve a safe person or qualified human support now. Do not isolate, drive yourself for urgent care, or return to ordinary rituals until safety is established.
URGENT OVERRIDE — HUMAN SUPPORT OVERRIDES THE RITUAL. If you may harm yourself or someone else, are in immediate danger, cannot stay safe, or may have a medical emergency, stop and contact local emergency services now. Australia: call 000. For 24/7 crisis support in Australia, call Lifeline 13 11 14 or text 0477 13 11 14. Outside Australia, use your local emergency or crisis service.

rituals.goal: Stop analysing the frightening experience and say the sentence that gets live help involved.
steps: Stop analysing what the experience means or why it started.
Call a trusted person, crisis service, or emergency responder.
Say, “My experience feels frightening and I need support now.”
Follow instructions that reduce risk and arrange assessment.
Keep the call or in-person contact active until help continues.
rituals.numbered_steps:
1. Stop analysing what the experience means or why it started.
2. Call a trusted person, crisis service, or emergency responder.
3. Say, “My experience feels frightening and I need support now.”
4. Follow instructions that reduce risk and arrange assessment.
5. Keep the call or in-person contact active until help continues.
rituals.win: A trusted person, crisis service, or emergency responder stayed connected and the next safety instructions came from outside the experience.
rituals.winReward: A trusted person, crisis service, or emergency responder stayed connected and the next safety instructions came from outside the experience.
tips: Have a trusted person stay nearby.
Lower nearby stimulation.
Avoid alcohol or recreational drugs.
Describe the experience without interpreting it.
